design_style: Orange-framed stand with a raised LED cube
materials_used: White laminate wall panels | Orange painted fin columns | LED video cube on four faces | Backlit graphic frames | Integrated planter boxes | Dark timber laminate flooring | Acrylic illuminated logo

01 The Challenge: Aatmanirbhar sells modules out of a 1.6 GW plant at Khargone, and 48 sqm on a two-side corner gives you very little wall to say that on. We put the exhibition stall design at REI Greater Noida to work vertically, because height is the one dimension a corner plot does not charge you for.
02 What We Designed: A four-sided LED cube sits a storey above the counter and runs factory footage over the heads of everyone in the aisle. Orange fins frame the bays below it, each one holding a backlit panel on capacity, warranty or the Kusum scheme. Planters are built into the feet of the columns. Inside, dark timber laminate and glass tables make a quieter room for the longer conversations.
03 Why It Worked: Height was the right place to spend the budget. The video reads from three aisles away, well before the fascia lettering resolves, and orange picks out of a hall where almost every solar stand is white or blue. At ground level the stall stays quiet enough to sit in, which is what the cabin and the timber floor are for.

design_style: Cream stand built around a large LED wall
materials_used: Cream laminate wall panels | Large LED video wall | Timber-framed module display bays | Backlit acrylic lettering | Faceted solid-surface counter | Printed module-pattern wall covering | Grey loop pile carpet

01 The Challenge: Citizen Solar came to REI with a 2.6 GW module line, a BSE listing and an ambassador campaign already shot. The job for the exhibition stall design at REI Greater Noida was to give all of that one place to land on 72 sqm without the stand turning into a poster wall.
02 What We Designed: The campaign film plays on a video wall that takes up most of the front elevation, so the stand moves even when nobody is standing at it. Above it a single band repeats the product claims across the whole fascia. Real modules sit in timber-lined bays along the side wall at 640 and 730 watts. The counter is faceted, cream with a thin gold line, and the lounge sits behind the display so conversations stay out of the aisle.
03 Why It Worked: Two things did the pulling. The film gave people a reason to stop without anyone having to approach them, and the module bays gave the sales team something to put a hand on once they had. Cream was a deliberate choice for a trade show booth in a hall of white and blue, and it photographs better than white under the hall lighting.

design_style: White portal frame outlined in warm light
materials_used: White laminate portal frame | Continuous warm LED strip | Backlit graphic bays | Circular illuminated logo discs | Timber reception counter | Wall-mounted module samples | Grey loop pile carpet

01 The Challenge: Contendre sells complete solar kits, so the pitch covers inverters, mounting and balance of system as much as the panel itself. Three open sides on 45 sqm left nowhere to hide a store, and the exhibition stall design at REI Greater Noida had to read as one object from every aisle while still carrying a full product story.
02 What We Designed: We drew one white portal around the whole plot and ran a warm LED strip along every edge of it, so the outline reads before any of the content does. Backlit bays fill the inside faces with module specs, warranty terms and the partner map. Illuminated discs carry the logo at two corners. A timber counter faces the main aisle, and the seating sits behind it on grey carpet.
03 Why It Worked: An outlined frame holds a three-side plot together in a way walls cannot, because there is nothing to walk around. The light line also gave the stand a recognisable silhouette at the far end of hall 14, which matters when the neighbours are larger. Visitors read the kit story on the way in, then sat down at the counter.

design_style: Compact white stand with an orange banded ceiling
materials_used: White laminate walls | Orange painted ceiling band | Backlit orange-framed panels | Glass display vitrine | White counters with a chevron detail | LED screen panel | Grey loop pile carpet

01 The Challenge: Elegant Green Energy makes balance of system parts, the cables, structures, panels and lighting that every solar plant needs and nobody photographs. On 27 sqm, the smallest plot we built at this show, the exhibition stall design at REI Greater Noida had to make a catalogue of components look like one coherent offer.
02 What We Designed: In a glass case on the front counter sits a scale model of a plant layout, wired and lit, so the components have somewhere to belong. Behind it a run of backlit panels in orange frames works through the ecosystem one application at a time. An orange band wraps the ceiling edge and ties a narrow plot together. A live control panel stands at the open corner.
03 Why It Worked: The model carries the stand. A box of cable glands and a switchgear panel are hard to care about on their own, and seeing them placed in a plant gives the sales conversation somewhere to start. Twenty-seven square metres is not much, so putting the one object worth looking at on the aisle counter was the whole plan.

01 The Challenge: A laser company at a renewable energy show has to explain itself before it can sell anything. IPG Photonics welds EV battery packs, a step most people at REI have never watched, so the exhibition stall design at REI Greater Noida was organised around the process, step by step.
02 What We Designed: The back wall runs the sequence left to right, from managing the details through process development and concept realisation to production support, with a real welding head and a robot arm on the counter at the end of it. Blue carpet printed with battery and vehicle icons marks the floor. A closed meeting room sits behind frosted glass, its walls carrying the two brand lines the company uses everywhere.
03 Why It Worked: Reading the wall takes about fifteen seconds and ends at a machine you can stand next to, which is roughly the attention a passing visitor gives an unfamiliar technology. The printed floor is the cheapest element on the stand and the one that answers the question a solar visitor arrives with, which is what a laser company is doing here at all.

title: Rayzon Solar Exhibition Stall Design at REI Greater Noida 2026
design_style: Curved cream double-decker with a sculpted fin structure
materials_used: Moulded cream fin structure | Illuminated oval fascia | Glazed mezzanine balustrade | Backlit fabric graphic wall | Frosted glass cabin doors | Fluted wall panelling | Polished white flooring
special_features: Mezzanine with meeting tables over the hall | Oval fascia with dimensional lettering | Sculpted fins around the perimeter | Row of air-conditioned meeting cabins | Backlit module display in a halo frame
01 The Challenge: Two hundred and twenty-eight square metres on four open sides, with a mezzanine on top, is the largest stand we have built for a solar client. Rayzon wanted private meeting space for distributors and an open floor for everyone else, and the exhibition stall design at REI Greater Noida had to hold both without one spoiling the other.
02 What We Designed: Nothing on the perimeter is square. Cream fins curve up into an oval fascia carrying dimensional letters, and the same curve repeats at the arched doors of the meeting cabins. The ground floor is bar tables and a backlit module in a halo frame. A staircase at the rear reaches the mezzanine, where more tables look down over the hall. Air conditioning, fluted panelling and a suspended ceiling make the cabins feel like rooms.
03 Why It Worked: The mezzanine solved the arithmetic. Floor space on a four-side island gets eaten by circulation, and putting the long meetings upstairs left the ground floor free to stay open on every edge. The upper tables sit far enough above the aisle to hold a conversation, which is difficult anywhere else on a four-side-open stall this busy.

design_style: White canopy stand edged in blue light
materials_used: Curved white fascia canopy | Blue LED cove lighting | Backlit graphic frames | Timber-framed fabric display | White product plinths | LED screen panel | Grey loop pile carpet
special_features: Blue light line under the plinth and canopy | Timber frame holding rolls of film | Plinths carrying ribbon and cable samples | Curved canopy over the open corner | Backlit panels on connection technology
01 The Challenge: Sekhani Renewables makes the parts of a module nobody sees, the ribbon that connects the cells and the film that seals them in. Selling an input to module makers on a 30 sqm plot is a different problem from selling a module, and the exhibition stall design at REI Greater Noida had to give those materials a shape people would walk towards.
02 What We Designed: Blue light runs as one continuous line under the plinth and again under the canopy, which curves out over the open corner. Spools of ribbon sit on white plinths at waist height where visitors can pick them up. A timber-framed case holds rolls of encapsulation film under the words Incredible World of Fabric. Backlit frames behind the seating cover connection technology and the production footprint.
03 Why It Worked: Component suppliers usually get a table and a banner. Giving the ribbon and the film their own lit furniture put them at the same level as the modules on the stands around them, and the blue line made a small stall legible from the aisle it shares with the China pavilion. Buyers could handle the product without asking.

title: Themis Automation Exhibition Stall Design at REI Greater Noida 2026
design_style: White stand built around a working water tank
materials_used: White laminate wall panels | Glass demonstration tank | Backlit specification frames | Illuminated acrylic lettering | White sideboard display units | LED screen panel | Grey loop pile carpet
special_features: Working solar pump running in a glass tank | Module canopy feeding the demonstration | Drives mounted beside the tank | Backlit panels on the pumping range | Lounge seating along the side wall
01 The Challenge: Themis Automation and Frecon sell solar pumping drives, a product that means nothing on a shelf and everything the moment it moves water. The exhibition stall design at REI Greater Noida was planned around one working demonstration, which is a risk on a 36 sqm plot because if it stops running there is nothing else to look at.
02 What We Designed: At the open corner stands a glass tank with a submersible pump in it, lit blue from below, under a canopy made from a real module. Two drives are mounted on the panel above the tank and wired to the pump, so the chain from sunlight to moving water is visible end to end. Behind it, backlit frames carry the drive range and the PCB solution, and more units sit on low white sideboards.
03 Why It Worked: A tank of moving water is rare on an exhibition floor, and it stops people walking. The demonstration also does the technical explaining on its own, which saves the engineers on the stand from describing a pumping curve to every visitor. Everything else here is deliberately plain so the tank stays the brightest object in view.

title: Valeo Exhibition Stall Design at REI Greater Noida 2026
design_style: Orange fascia over a white open frame
materials_used: White painted frame structure | Orange laminate fascia box | Glass display vitrines | Fluted timber accent wall | Backlit portrait lightbox | Timber laminate flooring | Frosted glass partitions
special_features: Glass vitrines holding interconnect spools | Backlit honeycomb logo on the fascia | Railed upper level above the fascia | Fluted timber wall behind the counter | Bar seating at the open corner
01 The Challenge: Valeo makes the tinned copper interconnect that joins the cells inside a solar module, which means the product is a reel of wire and the audience is every module maker in the hall. The exhibition stall design at REI Greater Noida had to make a reel of wire worth crossing an aisle for.
02 What We Designed: Two glass vitrines sit at the open corner on lit plinths with the spools inside them, which is how you display something small without it being picked up. An orange box carries the honeycomb logo above a white frame that leaves the sides open. A portrait lightbox explains the interconnect in one diagram. Behind the counter, fluted timber and a screen mark out the meeting area, and bar stools take the quick conversations.
03 Why It Worked: Orange was the useful decision. The hall runs white, blue and lime green carpet, so a terracotta box at fascia height is visible well before the logo resolves. Putting the spools in glass also changed how people treated them, because a component under a vitrine reads as engineered, which is the whole claim this trade show booth had to carry.

title: VSOLE Solar Exhibition Stall Design at REI Greater Noida 2026
design_style: Cream stand with LED walls and product bays
materials_used: Cream laminate wall panels | Large LED video walls | Backlit acrylic lettering | Frosted glass cabin doors | White product mounting panels | Polished white flooring | Timber-legged lounge furniture
special_features: Factory film running on two LED walls | Inverters mounted at eye level | Backlit counter at the corner | Row of enclosed meeting cabins | Floor-standing storage cabinets on display
01 The Challenge: VSOLE sells modules, inverters, batteries and a container-scale storage system, which is four product families competing for the same wall. Stall B419 gave us 66 sqm on three open sides, and the exhibition stall design at REI Greater Noida had to separate the ranges without cutting the plot into small rooms.
02 What We Designed: Each range gets its own wall. Inverters are mounted at eye level with their advantages printed beside them, batteries sit further along the same run, and the Storio cabinets stand on the floor where their size does the talking. Two LED walls play production footage from the factory at either end. Meeting cabins behind frosted glass take up the back edge, and the lounge furniture sits on polished white flooring.
03 Why It Worked: Wall-mounting the inverters is the detail that matters. An inverter on a table looks like a box, and an inverter on a wall at head height looks like the installed product, which is how a distributor sees it on a customer's wall. The factory film answers the manufacturing question before anyone asks it, and on a three-side-open stall the cabins kept distributor meetings off the floor.
